1	# proofpunk-agent
 2	
 3	A terminal mission-control UI for Claude Agent SDK sessions.
 4	
 5	`proofpunk-agent` drives a Claude Agent SDK session from a full-screen terminal
 6	interface and shows you what the session is actually doing while it does it: the
 7	agent tree as subagents fan out, assistant text as it streams, every tool call
 8	with its arguments and cost, every hook decision the Proofpunk plugin makes, the
 9	evidence run as it exists on disk, and a live performance budget.
10	
11	It is a *viewer with a keyboard*, not a wrapper that hides the SDK. Every screen
12	renders from one append-only event log projected out of the SDK stream; no widget
13	reads an SDK object directly, and no screen invents a number it did not measure.
14	Where a value is unavailable the UI renders `--` rather than a plausible
15	placeholder.
16	
17	---
18	
19	## Requirements
20	
21	- Python **3.10+** (developed and measured on 3.11.6)
22	- A terminal at least **100 x 28** — below that the app renders a blocking
23	  resize notice instead of a squeezed layout (`app.py:51-52`, `ResizeNotice`)
24	- A working Claude CLI installation, reachable by the SDK
25	- Optional but strongly recommended: a Proofpunk plugin checkout at **5.0.0 or
26	  newer** (see [Plugin root](#plugin-root))
27	
28	Pinned dependencies (`pyproject.toml:17-21`):
29	
30	```
31	claude-agent-sdk==0.2.144
32	textual==8.1.1
33	```
34	
35	## Install
36	
37	From a checkout:
38	
39	```sh
40	git clone https://github.com/krzemienski/proofpunk-agent
41	cd proofpunk-agent
42	python3 -m pip install -e .
43	```
44	
45	That installs the `proofpunk-agent` console script
46	(`pyproject.toml:23-24`). The module form works identically and is what the
47	validation harness uses:
48	
49	```sh
50	python3 -m proofpunk_agent --help
51	```
52	
53	Before starting a session, confirm which plugin root the resolver picked:
54	
55	```sh
56	python3 -m proofpunk_agent --check
57	```
58	
59	`--check` resolves the root, prints it with the precedence rung that produced
60	it, and exits without starting the UI. It exits `0` on success and `2` when no
61	candidate was accepted.
62	
63	---
64	
65	## CLI reference
66	
67	```
68	proofpunk-agent [-h] [--project PATH] [--model MODEL]
69	                [--effort {low,medium,high,max}] [--resume SESSION_ID]
70	                [--no-plugin] [--evidence-slug SLUG] [--version]
71	                [--proofpunk-path DIR]
72	                [--color-tier {truecolor,256,16}] [--theme NAME]
73	                [--max-budget USD] [--check]
74	                [PROMPT]
75	```
76	
77	| Flag | Argument | What it does |
78	| --- | --- | --- |
79	| `PROMPT` | positional, optional | Initial prompt. Omit it to start at the Screen 1 empty state. |
80	| `-h`, `--help` | — | Print usage and exit. |

1	"""P3 agent-tree reducer (§7 Screen 1 -- SESSION VIEW, Agent Tree panel).
  2	
  3	This module models the live agent hierarchy the tree panel renders: root
  4	orchestrator always node 0 (rule 1), children attaching by the §4
  5	attribution rule, per-node glyph state (rule 2), and the derived
  6	``active_count``/``max_depth`` figures the panel displays underneath the
  7	tree (rule 3).
  8	
  9	The attribution rule (§4, binding)
 10	-----------------------------------
 11	``events.py`` already carries the resolved attribution on every ``Event``:
 12	``event.parent`` (the linked parent id, or ``None``) and ``event.tier``
 13	(the ``AttributionTier`` that produced it). §4's strict preference order
 14	-- hook-provided ``agent_id``/``agent_type``, then ``parent_agent_id``,
 15	then ``parent_tool_use_id``, then the labeled ``(unattributed)`` fallback
 16	-- is therefore the PRODUCER's decision (the bridge that builds each
 17	``Event``, landing in Phase 3), not this reducer's. This reducer's only
 18	job is to APPLY that decision:
 19	
 20	- ``event.parent`` resolves to a node already in the tree -> attach there,
 21	  recording ``event.tier`` on the new node so the UI can render a
 22	  degraded-link label for anything below tier 1.
 23	- ``event.parent`` is ``None``, or names a node not present in the tree
 24	  (e.g. a genuinely unattributed spawn, or an out-of-order log) -> attach
 25	  under the root orchestrator and record ``AttributionTier.UNATTRIBUTED``.
 26	  This is the ONLY fallback path, and it is exactly the labeled
 27	  ``(unattributed)`` case §4 requires -- never a guess.
 28	
 29	No heuristic in this file infers a parent from event timing, name
 30	similarity, or proximity in the log. That is the prohibition §4 states
 31	explicitly, and the only way to satisfy it mechanically is to never write
 32	such a heuristic in the first place.
 33	
 34	Vocabulary ambiguity (documented, not guessed)
 35	-----------------------------------------------
 36	At this phase ``events.py`` defines the event kinds this reducer handles
 37	but not every field their payloads will carry once the Phase 3 bridge
 38	lands. Two gaps, resolved here the same way ``reduce_hooks`` resolves its
 39	own gaps -- by reading a documented key out of ``event.data``/``event.parent``
 40	rather than inventing new ``EventKind`` members:
 41	
 42	- **Owning agent for a tool call or permission prompt.** ``TOOL_STARTED``,
 43	  ``TOOL_FINISHED``, ``PERMISSION_REQUESTED``, and ``PERMISSION_RESOLVED``
 44	  all describe something that belongs to a running agent, not the agent
 45	  itself (``event.subject`` is the tool-use id or permission id). This
 46	  reducer reads the owning agent as ``event.parent`` if set, falling back
 47	  to ``event.data["agent_id"]``. An event that resolves neither is
 48	  ignored for tree purposes (documented below), never applied to a
 49	  guessed node.
 50	- **Success vs failure on ``AGENT_FINISHED``.** Resolved via
 51	  ``event.data.get("error")`` (truthy) or
 52	  ``event.data.get("status") in {"error", "errored"}`` -> ``ERRORED``;
 53	  otherwise -> ``COMPLETE``.
 54	
 55	Ignored event kinds
 56	--------------------
 57	``ASSISTANT_TEXT``, ``HOOK_EVENT``, ``TASK_UPDATED``, ``RESULT``, and
 58	``ERROR`` do not carry tree-shape information at this phase (``ERROR`` is
 59	system/ledger-scoped; see ``reduce_hooks``'s own documented vocabulary).
 60	They fall through the reducer's final ``else`` and return ``state``
 61	unchanged -- an explicit, total no-op, never an unhandled branch.
 62	
 63	``IDLE`` (§7 Screen 1 rule 2) is a valid ``NodeState`` value with no
 64	producing transition in this phase: no handled event kind conveys "an
 65	agent is idle" yet. It exists so the UI's glyph table is complete and so
 66	a future event kind can target it without a reducer-shape change.
 67	"""
 68	
 69	from __future__ import annotations
 70	
 71	from dataclasses import dataclass, field, replace
 72	from enum import Enum
 73	from types import MappingProxyType
 74	from typing import Mapping
 75	
 76	from proofpunk_agent.state.events import AttributionTier, Event, EventKind
 77	
 78	__all__ = [
 79	    "NodeState",
 80	    "TreeNode",
 81	    "TreeState",
 82	    "ROOT_AGENT_ID",
 83	    "EMPTY_TREE_STATE",
 84	    "reduce_tree",
 85	]
 86	
 87	#: Root orchestrator's fixed node id (§7 Screen 1 rule 1: "root orchestrator
 88	#: always node 0"). A constant rather than a value read off the SDK session
 89	#: id keeps this reducer independent of the bridge's session-naming choices.
 90	ROOT_AGENT_ID: str = "orchestrator"
 91	
 92	
 93	class NodeState(str, Enum):
 94	    """§7 Screen 1 rule 2 glyph states."""
 95	
 96	    RUNNING = "running"
 97	    PERMISSION_PENDING = "permission_pending"
 98	    IDLE = "idle"
 99	    COMPLETE = "complete"
100	    ERRORED = "errored"
101	
102	
103	@dataclass(frozen=True)
104	class TreeNode:
105	    """One agent-tree node: identity, display state, and linkage.
106	
107	    ``attribution`` records the ``AttributionTier`` that produced
108	    ``parent_id`` (§4) so the UI can render the degraded-link label for
109	    anything below ``HOOK_AGENT_ID``. ``depth`` is cached at attach time
110	    (``parent.depth + 1``) rather than recomputed by walking ``parent_id``
111	    chains -- the tree only grows forward through this reducer, so a
112	    node's depth is fixed the moment it is attached.
113	    """
114	
115	    agent_id: str
116	    name: str
117	    state: NodeState
118	    parent_id: str | None
119	    attribution: AttributionTier
120	    depth: int
121	    children: tuple[str, ...] = ()
122	    current_tool: str | None = None
123	
124	
125	def _root_node() -> TreeNode:
126	    return TreeNode(
127	        agent_id=ROOT_AGENT_ID,
128	        name="orchestrator",
129	        state=NodeState.RUNNING,
130	        parent_id=None,
131	        attribution=AttributionTier.HOOK_AGENT_ID,
132	        depth=0,
133	        children=(),
134	        current_tool=None,
135	    )
136	
137	
138	@dataclass(frozen=True)
139	class TreeState:
140	    """Full P3 hierarchy, keyed by ``agent_id``.
141	
142	    ``nodes`` is a ``MappingProxyType`` rather than a plain ``dict``: a
143	    frozen dataclass stops reassignment of the ``nodes`` attribute, but
144	    without the proxy a caller holding the dict object could still mutate
145	    it in place, silently corrupting a state some other part of the app
146	    (or a replay) still references.
147	    """
148	
149	    nodes: Mapping[str, TreeNode] = field(
150	        default_factory=lambda: MappingProxyType({})
151	    )
152	
153	    @property
154	    def root(self) -> TreeNode | None:
155	        return self.nodes.get(ROOT_AGENT_ID)
156	
157	    @property
158	    def active_count(self) -> int:
159	        """§7 Screen 1 rule 3: nodes currently in the ``running`` state."""
160	        return sum(1 for n in self.nodes.values() if n.state is NodeState.RUNNING)
161	
162	    @property
163	    def max_depth(self) -> int:
164	        """§7 Screen 1 rule 3: deepest attached node, 0 if only (or not
165	        even) the root exists."""
166	        if not self.nodes:
167	            return 0
168	        return max(n.depth for n in self.nodes.values())
169	
170	
171	EMPTY_TREE_STATE = TreeState()
172	
173	
174	def _put(state: TreeState, node: TreeNode) -> TreeState:
175	    """Return a new ``TreeState`` with ``node`` inserted/replaced."""
176	    updated = dict(state.nodes)
177	    updated[node.agent_id] = node
178	    return replace(state, nodes=MappingProxyType(updated))
179	
180	
181	def _ensure_root(state: TreeState) -> TreeState:
182	    """Guarantee a root node exists before any attach/update.
183	
184	    Events are expected in order (``SESSION_INIT`` first), but a reducer
185	    must stay total against a malformed or out-of-order log rather than
186	    raising ``KeyError`` deep in an attach step -- an implicit root keeps
187	    every later operation well-defined without ever guessing a parent.
188	    """
189	    if ROOT_AGENT_ID in state.nodes:
190	        return state
191	    return _put(state, _root_node())
192	
193	
194	def _resolve_owner(state: TreeState, event: Event) -> str | None:
195	    """Owning agent for a tool/permission event (documented above):
196	    ``event.parent`` first, then ``event.data["agent_id"]``, then

198	    candidate = event.parent or event.data.get("agent_id")

205	    node = state.nodes.get(agent_id)
206	    if node is None:
207	        return state
208	    return _put(state, replace(node, state=new_state))

212	    state: TreeState, agent_id: str, current_tool: str | None
213	) -> TreeState:

no assertions framework, no ``test_``-prefixed anything, and no mock/stub/fake

end-user-testing claim can cite. Textual's own headless Pilot-driving entry

calling process owns a terminal, so it can never stand in for "driven in a
real PTY". That identifier is deliberately never spelled out literally in this
module, so a plain-substring search against this file returns zero hits.

Why this module is not ``script -qfc``
--------------------------------------
``scenario_session.py``'s docstring names a ``script -qfc`` fallback path and
records that it was never implemented. Measured on this host before writing
anything, that path is not merely unimplemented -- it is unavailable and
unfit:

  * ``script -qfc`` is **util-linux** syntax. This host is Darwin; its BSD
    ``script`` advertises ``[-aeFkpqr] [-t time] [file [command ...]]`` -- no
    ``-c``, no ``-f``. The flags do not exist to be passed.
  * BSD ``script`` hands its child a **0x0 window**: a child running
    ``stty size`` under it reports ``0 0``. A product with a 100x28 floor
    cannot be driven through a terminal that claims no size at all.
  * Wrapped inside a correctly-sized PTY it still does **not propagate later
    size changes**: after the master was resized 100x28 -> 60x20 the child kept
    reporting ``28 100``. Retried with ``SIGWINCH`` to the process group AND to
    the ``script`` pid directly, with a 1.5s settle. No propagation either way.

resize fuzzing, which is most of what a fallback would be needed for. So this
module implements the same *contract* -- a real PTY, addressable by the same
surface ``PtySession`` presents -- on ``pty.fork()`` instead.

Why ``pty.fork()``
------------------
``pty.fork()`` makes the child a session leader with the slave as its
**controlling terminal**. That is what ``script`` was being asked to provide
